evals.description: AL2023 rpmdb.sqlite is totally corrupt; skill must recognize that rpm --rebuilddb leaves an empty DB and the inventory must be rebuilt from repos (initdb + dnf reinstall), not rebuilddb.
evals.prompt: On an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance, dnf patching fails with 'error: rpmdb open failed' and 'cannot open Packages index using sqlite: file is not a database'. I ran `rpm --rebuilddb` and it completed, but now `rpm -qa` returns 0 packages. How do I recover this so patching works?
evals.expected_output: Explains that on AL2023 (sqlite backend) rpm --rebuilddb rebuilds the index from the on-disk package headers, so when rpmdb.sqlite is totally corrupt ('file is not a database') there are no headers to rebuild from and the DB ends up empty. The correct recovery is to reconstruct the inventory from the repositories: rpm --initdb, then dnf reinstall the packages (e.g. system-release first, then '*' with --skip-broken) and dnf distro-sync, after backing up /var/lib/rpm. Notes rpm --rebuilddb cannot recover this total-loss case.
assertions: Explains that rpm --rebuilddb leaves an empty database because there are no on-disk headers to rebuild from when the sqlite file is totally corrupt
Recommends reconstructing the package inventory from the repositories (initdb + dnf reinstall) rather than rpm --rebuilddb
Recommends backing up /var/lib/rpm before mutating it
Does not recommend simply re-running rpm --rebuilddb as the fix

evals.description: Corrupt RPM DB; skill must detect backend (sqlite vs BerkeleyDB) and apply the correct recovery rather than a blind rebuilddb.
evals.prompt: A Linux fleet has patch failures with 'rpmdb: BDB0113 Thread/process failed' on some hosts and 'database disk image is malformed' on others. What is the correct way to recover the RPM database across these hosts?
evals.expected_output: Explains the recovery depends on the RPM backend: BerkeleyDB hosts (AL2, RHEL7/8, CentOS7, OL7, SLES12) have Packages + __db.* — drop the cached __db.* environment files then rpm --rebuilddb; SQLite hosts (AL2023, RHEL9, OL9, SLES15) have rpmdb.sqlite — move the corrupt sqlite aside and rebuild, and if totally corrupt reconstruct from repos. Detect the backend first (check for rpmdb.sqlite vs Packages/__db.*), clear stale locks, and back up /var/lib/rpm before rebuilding. A BerkeleyDB-only fix does not recover a corrupt sqlite DB and vice versa.
assertions: Distinguishes the SQLite backend recovery from the BerkeleyDB backend recovery
Recommends detecting which backend is in use before choosing the recovery
Recommends backing up /var/lib/rpm and clearing stale locks before rebuilding
Does not prescribe a single backend-agnostic command for all hosts

evals.description: dpkg status parse error; skill must restore from status-old (distinct from clearing the updates/ journal).
evals.prompt: On an Ubuntu 22.04 EC2 instance, apt/patching fails with: dpkg: parsing file '/var/lib/dpkg/status' near line 14477 package 'zstd': end of file during value of field 'Homepage' (missing final newline), and 'dpkg was interrupted, you must manually run dpkg --configure -a'. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that /var/lib/dpkg/status is corrupt (truncated stanza / missing final newline), which is different from corrupt journal files in /var/lib/dpkg/updates/. The fix is to back up the current status, restore /var/lib/dpkg/status from /var/lib/dpkg/status-old (the known-good copy dpkg writes on each successful update), then run dpkg --configure -a and apt-get install -f. Notes that if status-old is missing/empty this must be escalated (possible snapshot restore).
assertions: Recommends restoring /var/lib/dpkg/status from status-old for a corrupt status file
Distinguishes a corrupt dpkg status file from corrupt journal files in /var/lib/dpkg/updates/
Recommends backing up the current status file before restoring
Notes escalation if status-old is missing or empty
